Statement by the Director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure). is with a profound sense of purpose that I present our Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for this year. At the heart of the Company lies a simple yet powerful conviction: 'recycle today, greener tomorrow'. We are not merely a non-ferrous metal recycling enterprise; we are a dedicated circular economy business driven by a genuine responsibility to safeguard our environment for future generations. Our environmental stewardship is a commitment we hold deeply. We are actively decoupling our growth from environmental impact by transitioning to renewable solar energy and rigorously upholding our pledge to zero discharge, zero landfill, and zero burning manufacturing. By innovating to recover valuable by-products from our core processes, we ensure that what might otherwise be discarded is respectfully transformed back into vital resources. Beyond our operational footprint, we care deeply about the people and communities we touch. We are actively nurturing the next generation by elevating educational infrastructure and providing support to aspiring students. We remain equally devoted to empowering underprivileged women, advocating for animal welfare, and, crucially, fostering a dignified, safe, and inclusive workplace for every individual within the Company. We anchor these ambitions in uncompromising governance. Guided by independent Board oversight, ethical transparency forms the absolute bedrock of our operations. As we look ahead, we warmly welcome India’s evolving sustainability landscape. We are proactively aligning our strategies to champion the forthcoming Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations taking effect from April 2026, as well as future recycled content mandates. We remain resolute in building a resilient enterprise that thrives on the lasting, positive impact we leave behind.

While e-waste recycling is not the Company’s primary business, discarded electrical and electronic equipment, such as computers, televisions, mobile phones and washing machines, is occasionally received within imported scrap consignments. Such e-waste is transferred to government-authorised recyclers for collection, segregation, treatment, recycling and environmentally sound disposal in accordance with applicable regulations.

The Company’s operations involve handling hazardous materials, primarily used lead-acid batteries and the resulting sulphuric acid electrolyte. Automated battery-breaking systems safely recover lead, plastic and electrolyte. The electrolyte is neutralised and treated for safe disposal or suitable industrial reuse, while hazardous waste is managed through authorised agencies in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.

Residual waste streams are processed using technologies such as vacuum distillation, magnetic separation and eddy current separation to recover valuable metals, including tin and iron. Cross-facility utilisation of by-products and zero-discharge initiatives further minimise waste generation and ensure that only non-recyclable waste is disposed of through authorised channels.

Plastic is recovered as a by-product of the Company’s lead and copper recycling operations in the form of PPCP chips and PVC grind. These materials are processed through crushing, washing, separation and extrusion to produce recycled PPCP and PVC granules, which are reused in applications such as packaging, automotive components, footwear and garden pipes. The Company is also establishing a dedicated plastic recycling facility to further strengthen its recycling capabilities.
